title: CRASH-120: unserialize object_common1 cursor advance past truncated buffer oob read (out-of-bounds-read)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow at ext/standard/var_unserializer.c:195 in finish_nested_data when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 16b3003ffc63, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/var_unserializer.c:208-210 (defect, object_common1) == ext/standard/var_unserializer.re:213-215; OOB read surfaces at ext/standard/var_unserializer.c:195 (finish_nested_data)
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has finish_nested_data at ext/standard/var_unserializer.c:195 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the nested layer present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
